data.description:
## Incident Overview

When merge-to-main.sh runs in PR mode and the PR auto-merges as a squash commit, the script's subsequent auto-bump phase commits a version bump (1.17.5→1.17.6) to **local** main, but the local main pointer is still at the pre-merge base. Origin/main has moved to the squash-merge commit (a different SHA from the local merge), so the bump commit is on a stale base and the push fails with non-fast-forward. Each --resume creates ANOTHER bump commit (1.17.6→1.17.7→…) on the same stale base instead of rebasing local main onto origin/main first, accumulating orphan commits indefinitely.

## Observed (session 2026-05-16)

- PR #150 auto-merged successfully (squash) as origin/main 9ad7108e2e
- Script bumped 1.17.5 → 1.17.6 on local main and tried to push → non-fast-forward
- --resume bumped 1.17.6 → 1.17.7 on the **same** stale base and tried to push → non-fast-forward again
- Local main now has two orphan bump commits not on origin

## Expected

After PR auto-merge, the bump phase should fetch origin/main, reset/rebase local main onto it, then bump on top, then push. --resume should detect existing orphan bump commits and either rebase them onto fresh origin/main or discard and re-create.

## Also

merge-to-main.sh --help says '(no args) Run all phases sequentially (no version bump).' but invocation with no args produced 'INFO: --bump not specified — defaulting to patch (version.file_path configured).' Help text and behavior disagree. Pick one.
data.title: [merge-to-main.sh PR-mode]: post-merge auto-bump commits on stale local main -> push rejected non-fast-forward, --resume creates additional orphan bumps each iteration
